race_context: Nettle Creek School Corporation is based in Hagerstown in western Wayne County and runs two schools: Hagerstown Elementary (preschool through grade 6) and Hagerstown Jr.-Sr. High School (grades 7-12), with about 1,100 students {nc_who}. Enrollment was about 1,071 as of July 24, 2026, ahead of the official Oct. 1 count {wwn_finance_aug}. The state ballot names for these offices add '(Wayne-Henry)', indicating the district reaches into Henry County {in_list}. Superintendent: Emily Schaeffer {wwn_officers26}{wwn_president24}.

The board has seven members: four at-large seats and one seat each for Districts A, B and C {nc_board}. Current members are Shaun Lieberman (at large, president), Sandi Schraub (at large, vice president), Julie Blaase (District A, secretary), Ruthie LaMar (at large), Marcie Houghton (at large), Cody Sankey (District B) and Mike Banning (District C) {nc_board}{wwn_officers26}. Candidates file a petition signed by at least 10 voters in their board district {wwn_filing}{wwn_filing_rules}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: two at-large seats and the District B seat, which covers Dalton and Perry townships {wwn_slate}{wwn_filing}. The state list shows the at-large race as 'vote for 1', but the Western Wayne News reported two at-large seats open, matching the two seats held by Lieberman and Houghton, whose terms were last up in 2022 {wwn_slate}{pi_2022}{in_list}. All three incumbents filed again and none has an opponent: Houghton (Republican) and Lieberman (nonpartisan) for the two at-large seats and Sankey (Republican) for District B {wwn_slate}.

Budget cuts (May 2026): facing a projected $623,000 gap between revenue and spending, which the newspaper tied to lower enrollment and state funding pressures, the board voted 6-0 at a May 27 special meeting to cut about $612,000 from the education fund, including two cancelled teacher contracts, four unfilled vacancies and six instructional assistant positions, plus custodial, maintenance and transportation cuts in the operations fund; Houghton was absent {wwn_cuts}. An earlier work session aimed to save about $300,000 in the operations fund for 2026-27 {wwn_worksession}.

Finances (2025-2026): there were no raises in 2025 because of fund reappropriations, and a wage increase was a 2026 goal {wwn_officers26}. In February 2025 board member Sandi Schraub urged residents to read Senate Bill 1, the property-tax bill, saying it would affect schools and local governments {wwn_lawmakers}. By July 2026 the operations fund was out of the red at $883,176, and two reduced teaching positions were reinstated; each student brings about $7,345 in state funding {wwn_finance_aug}.

Facilities and policy: an architectural firm's facility assessments are guiding a 10-year building and maintenance plan, and in July 2026 the board updated policies under the new state wireless device ban {wwn_finance_aug}. Blaase noted the district's 100% graduation rate in 2025 {wwn_officers26}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum or questionnaire for these uncontested races. The Western Wayne News ran candidate Q&As for contested Nettle Creek races in 2020 and 2024, but none for 2026 was found {wwn_qa2020}{wwn_qa2024}.
